investigator.method: Bounded Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC probe as part of BEATMAPPED-LONDON-SECOND-LIVE-TRANCHE-01 triage refinement: a single unauthenticated GET to the venue's official website (or official programme URL when directly given), no retries, no browser, no authentication, no challenge bypass, no state-changing request.

probe_history.reason: The retained Level 1 listing proves Wilton's Music Hall is a genuinely mixed theatre/music/cabaret venue rather than resolving cleanly to either side of the music gate; a bounded per-event pass (or a fuller listing fetch) is needed before a READY_FOR_OFFLINE_PROOF or REJECT decision would be honest.

identity.notes: The retained response's own page title is "What's On - Wilton's Music Hall" and its What's On listing markup (WhatsOnList/WhatsonItem classes) is served directly from wiltons.org.uk, matching the candidate name and Graces Alley, E1 8JB address.

venue_location.notes: The retained response's own address text corroborates the candidate's discovery-supplied address, but this probe did not promote it to a canonical venue fact.

reasons: The retained What's On listing is genuinely mixed: current/upcoming titles directly present in the response include the opera "The Elixir of Love", the live-scored silent films "The Cabinet of Dr Caligari (1920) with live score" and "Harold Lloyd's Safety Last! (1923) with live score", the words-and-music show "INCENDIARY – Samuel Pepys in Words and Music", and the musical-revue cabaret "FLOP! The Best Songs From The Worst Musicals" — all substantially musical performance.

The same listing also includes plays ("The Signalman", "Private Peaceful"), stand-up/spoken word ("Tim Key: Loganberry", "Phil Ellis – Bath Mat", "A Brief Case of Crazy") and a non-performance history tour, so the primary programme cannot be honestly called substantially music without deeper per-event classification of the full current listing.

evidence.description: Retained, bounded, contiguous excerpt of the actual HTTP response body from the single unauthenticated GET, plus real response metadata (status, final URL, content-type); the excerpt substring is a literal transcription of the response but is wrapped in a JSON envelope with metadata rather than the full raw byte stream, so it is not itself the byte-faithful response.
evidence.method: curl -sL; descriptive research User-Agent; 20-second timeout; redirects followed; unauthenticated GET; no retry.
